title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a set of notes on the 'surgery of conformal surfaces'. It fixes the setting and states the standard criterion for a Riemann surface to be hyperbolic.

Setting. X is a holomorphic surface (a Riemann surface), connected ('0-connexe'), not necessarily compact, and separated (Hausdorff). X̃ is its universal cover.

Theorem: the following conditions are equivalent.
(i) X is not isomorphic to any of P^1_C, A^1_C = P^1 minus {∞}, G_m = P^1 minus {0,∞}, or a complex elliptic curve.
(ii) X̃ is isomorphic to the Poincaré upper half-plane H.
(iii) Every holomorphic map C → X is constant (Brody/Liouville–Picard hyperbolicity).
(iv) If X is an open subset of a complex projective line, then the complement has cardinality ≥ 3. If X is an open subset of a complex affine line, the complement has cardinality ≥ 2.
(v) If X = X̂ minus S, with X̂ compact of genus g and S finite of cardinality ν, then 2g+ν ≥ 3. Equivalently (g,ν) ∉ {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0)}, i.e. χ(X) < 0.

Definition. Such an X is called hyperbolic.

Corollary 1. A connected open subset of a hyperbolic surface is hyperbolic.

Corollary 2. If X is a connected holomorphic surface with boundary and ∂X ≠ ∅, then Int X is hyperbolic.

Role in the notes. All of this follows from Koebe–Poincaré uniformization (X̃ ∈ {P^1, C, H}) together with the classification of quotients of P^1 and C. The page sets up the trichotomy that the next pages use:
- the next page treats non-orientable conformal surfaces (RP^2, and real genus-1 curves without real points modulo conjugation);
- it then defines the canonical metric on a conformal surface, starting with the hyperbolic case (curvature −1, obtained by descent from H).

The page is preparatory for a programme of 'conformal surgery', which elsewhere connects to Grothendieck's work on dessins and maps (cartes).
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence 2g+ν≥3 ⇔ (g,ν) not in the four excluded cases ⇔ χ = 2−2g−ν < 0 is correct.

(iv) is stated only for open subsets of P^1 or A^1, and (v) only for finite-type surfaces. These are conditional reformulations under extra hypotheses, not full equivalents in general. This is correctly signalled by the square brackets.
Corollary 2 implicitly needs the boundary to be analytic, so that X embeds in a slightly larger open Riemann surface. This is standard.

ideas.what: Characterization of hyperbolic Riemann surfaces: universal cover is H; no nonconstant entire curves; complement of at least 3 points in P^1; χ<0 for finite type
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization theorem / hyperbolic Riemann surfaces (Brody hyperbolicity in dimension 1, Picard theorem)
ideas.where_published: Implicit background in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discussion of hyperbolic curves (g,ν) with 2g+ν>2

ideas.what: Open connected subsets of hyperbolic surfaces are hyperbolic; interiors of bordered surfaces are hyperbolic
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity of hyperbolicity / bordered Riemann surfaces

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but entirely classical statement of the uniformization trichotomy and its corollaries. It is preparatory material for the conformal-surgery notes, with no new content on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'o-connexe' is most likely '0-connexe' (Grothendieck's notation for connected).
In (iv), the crossed-out letters inside card(...) appear to be corrected symbols, probably P^1 ∖ X and A^1 ∖ X. They should not be read as X' ∖ X.
In (v), the insertions read 'genre g' (above X̂) and 'card ν' (above S). The trailing '[?] X'' is spurious.
